functions.name: mpc_err_delete
functions.description: Destroy and free an mpc_err_t error object returned in mpc_result_t on parse failure.
requirements: e must be a valid pointer to an error produced by MPC (e.g., from mpc_result_t on failure).
After calling, the error is invalid and must not be used.

functions.name: mpc_err_string
functions.description: Render an mpc_err_t into a newly-allocated human-readable C string for diagnostics.
requirements: e must be a valid pointer to an MPC error.
The returned string is heap-allocated and must be freed by the caller (free).

functions.name: mpc_err_print
functions.description: Print a human-readable description of an MPC error to stderr.
requirements: e must be a valid pointer to an MPC error.

functions.name: mpc_err_print_to
functions.description: Print a human-readable description of an MPC error to the given FILE stream.
requirements: e must be a valid pointer to an MPC error.
f must be a valid, open FILE* for writing.

functions.name: mpc_parse
functions.signature: int mpc_parse(const char *filename, const char *string, mpc_parser_t *p, mpc_result_t *r);
functions.description: Parse a NUL-terminated input string with parser p. On success, r->output is set; on failure, r->error is set.
requirements: filename must be a valid C string used for diagnostics (may be a virtual name).
string must be a valid NUL-terminated input buffer.
p must point to a valid parser (typically from mpc_new/builders).
r must be a non-NULL pointer to an mpc_result_t storage provided by caller.
Caller must inspect the return value to distinguish success/failure and then free either r->output (with appropriate destructor) or r->error (with mpc_err_delete) accordingly.

functions.name: mpc_nparse
functions.signature: int mpc_nparse(const char *filename, const char *string, size_t length, mpc_parser_t *p, mpc_result_t *r);
functions.description: Parse an input buffer with explicit length using parser p. On success fills r->output; on failure fills r->error.
requirements: filename must be a valid C string for diagnostics.
string must point to a buffer of at least length bytes (may contain NULs).
length is the number of bytes to parse from string.
p must be a valid parser.
r must be non-NULL and writable.
Caller must check return value and free either r->output or r->error appropriately.

functions.name: mpc_parse_file
functions.signature: int mpc_parse_file(const char *filename, FILE *file, mpc_parser_t *p, mpc_result_t *r);
functions.description: Parse all contents of an open FILE* using parser p. On success r->output is set; on failure r->error is set.
requirements: filename is used for diagnostics and must be a valid C string.
file must be a valid readable FILE* positioned at the start of the content to parse (library will read from it).
p must be a valid parser.
r must be non-NULL and writable.
Caller must check return and free result or error accordingly.

functions.name: mpc_parse_pipe
functions.signature: int mpc_parse_pipe(const char *filename, FILE *pipe, mpc_parser_t *p, mpc_result_t *r);
functions.description: Parse from a FILE* treated as a pipe/stream using parser p. On success r->output is set; on failure r->error is set.
requirements: filename is for diagnostics and must be a valid C string.
pipe must be a valid readable FILE* stream.
p must be a valid parser.
r must be non-NULL and writable.
Caller must check return and free result or error accordingly.

functions.name: mpc_parse_contents
functions.description: Open and parse the contents of a file given by filename using parser p. On success r->output is set; on failure r->error is set.
requirements: filename must be a valid path to a readable file.
p must be a valid parser.
r must be non-NULL and writable.
Caller must check return and free result or error accordingly.

functions.name: mpc_new
functions.description: Create a new named parser placeholder/forward declaration that can later be defined and combined with combinators.
requirements: name must be a valid C string used to label the parser.

functions.name: mpc_copy
functions.description: Create a copy/clone of an existing parser a.
requirements: a must be a valid parser pointer.

functions.name: mpc_define
functions.description: Define the body/implementation of parser p to be parser a (used for recursive or forward-declared grammars).
requirements: p must be a parser created by mpc_new (a placeholder).
a must be a valid parser representing the definition.
Do not use p before it has been defined.

functions.name: mpc_undefine
functions.description: Remove the definition from parser p, turning it back into an undefined placeholder.
requirements: p must be a valid parser pointer, typically previously defined with mpc_define.

functions.name: mpc_delete
functions.description: Destroy and free a parser and any associated resources.
requirements: p must be a valid parser pointer.
Do not use p after deletion.

functions.name: mpc_cleanup
functions.description: Convenience function to delete/free multiple parsers/resources in one call; typically passed the number of parsers followed by that many mpc_parser_t* pointers.
requirements: n must equal the count of subsequent variadic arguments.
Each variadic argument must be a valid pointer of the expected type (commonly mpc_parser_t*).

functions.name: mpc_any
functions.description: Parser that consumes any single character.

functions.name: mpc_char
functions.description: Parser that matches exactly the given character c.

functions.name: mpc_range
functions.description: Parser that matches a character within the inclusive range [s, e].

functions.name: mpc_oneof
functions.description: Parser that matches any one character from the set provided in string s.
requirements: s must be a valid NUL-terminated C string.

functions.name: mpc_noneof
functions.description: Parser that matches any single character not included in the set s.
requirements: s must be a valid NUL-terminated C string.

functions.name: mpc_satisfy
functions.description: Parser that consumes one character iff predicate f(c) returns non-zero.
requirements: f must be a valid function pointer taking a char and returning int (non-zero = match).

functions.name: mpc_string
functions.description: Parser that matches the exact string s.
requirements: s must be a valid NUL-terminated C string.

functions.name: mpc_pass
functions.description: Parser that always succeeds without consuming input, usually yielding a null/placeholder value.

functions.name: mpc_fail
functions.description: Parser that always fails with the given static message m.
requirements: m must be a valid C string describing the failure.

functions.name: mpc_failf
functions.description: Parser that always fails with a formatted message constructed from printf-style fmt and variadic args.
requirements: fmt must be a valid printf-style format string.
Variadic arguments must match fmt.

functions.name: mpc_lift
functions.description: Parser that produces a value by invoking constructor f without consuming input.
requirements: f must be a valid function pointer returning mpc_val_t*.

functions.name: mpc_lift_val
functions.description: Parser that yields the provided value x without consuming input.
requirements: x must be a valid pointer to a value with an agreed lifetime/ownership per surrounding combinators.

functions.name: mpc_anchor
functions.description: Anchor parser that succeeds based on a predicate over previous and next characters; used for word boundaries or similar.
requirements: f must be a valid function pointer taking (prev, next) chars, returning non-zero to allow a match.

functions.name: mpc_state
functions.description: Parser that yields the current input state (position/row/col) without consuming input.

functions.name: mpc_expect
functions.description: Wrap parser a to override its error message with e on failure.
requirements: a must be a valid parser.
e must be a valid C string used in errors.

functions.name: mpc_expectf
functions.description: Wrap parser a to override its error message with a formatted string built from fmt and args.
requirements: a must be a valid parser.
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string; variadic args must match.

functions.name: mpc_apply
functions.description: Apply a post-processing function f to the value produced by parser a.
requirements: a must be a valid parser that produces a value compatible with f.
f must be a valid function pointer taking and returning mpc_val_t*.

functions.name: mpc_apply_to
functions.description: Apply a post-processing function f with user data x to the value produced by parser a.
requirements: a must be a valid parser that produces a value compatible with f.
f must be a valid function pointer of type mpc_apply_to_t.
x is an opaque pointer passed to f and must remain valid during parsing.

functions.name: mpc_check
functions.signature: mpc_parser_t *mpc_check(mpc_parser_t *a, mpc_dtor_t da, mpc_check_t f, const char *e);
functions.description: Validate the value from parser a with predicate f; on failure, free with da and report error message e.
requirements: a must be a valid parser.
da must be a valid destructor for values produced by a (or mpcf_dtor_null).
f must be a valid predicate taking mpc_val_t** and returning non-zero on success.
e must be a valid C string for the error message.

functions.name: mpc_check_with
functions.signature: mpc_parser_t *mpc_check_with(mpc_parser_t *a, mpc_dtor_t da, mpc_check_with_t f, void *x, const char *e);
functions.description: Like mpc_check but passes user data x to predicate f.
requirements: a must be a valid parser.
da must correctly free values from a.
f must be a valid predicate of type mpc_check_with_t.
x must remain valid for the duration of the check.
e must be a valid C string for the error message.

functions.name: mpc_checkf
functions.signature: mpc_parser_t *mpc_checkf(mpc_parser_t *a, mpc_dtor_t da, mpc_check_t f, const char *fmt, ...);
functions.description: Like mpc_check but with a formatted error message built from fmt and args.
requirements: a, da, f as per mpc_check.
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string; variadic args must match.

functions.name: mpc_check_withf
functions.signature: mpc_parser_t *mpc_check_withf(mpc_parser_t *a, mpc_dtor_t da, mpc_check_with_t f, void *x, const char *fmt, ...);
functions.description: Like mpc_check_with but with a formatted error message.
requirements: a, da, f, x as per mpc_check_with.
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string; variadic args must match.

functions.name: mpc_not
functions.description: Negative lookahead: succeeds when a would fail at the current position; does not consume input; frees any produced value with da if needed.
requirements: a must be a valid parser.
da must be a valid destructor for a's value (or mpcf_dtor_null).

functions.name: mpc_not_lift
functions.description: Negative lookahead that, on success, produces a value by calling lf.
requirements: a must be a valid parser.
da must properly free a's value (or be null dtor).
lf must be a valid constructor function.

functions.name: mpc_maybe
functions.description: Optional: tries a; on failure, succeeds without consuming input and typically yields a null value.
requirements: a must be a valid parser.

functions.name: mpc_maybe_lift
functions.description: Optional with default: tries a; on failure, succeeds producing a value from lf.
requirements: a must be a valid parser.
lf must be a valid constructor.

functions.name: mpc_many
functions.description: Repetition: parse zero or more occurrences of a and fold them with f into a single value.
requirements: a must be a valid parser.
f must be a valid fold function combining n values into one.

functions.name: mpc_many1
functions.description: Repetition: parse one or more occurrences of a and fold them with f.
requirements: a must be a valid parser.
f must be a valid fold function.

functions.name: mpc_count
functions.signature: mpc_parser_t *mpc_count(int n, mpc_fold_t f, mpc_parser_t *a, mpc_dtor_t da);
functions.description: Parse exactly n occurrences of a; fold them with f; use da to free intermediates on failure.
requirements: n must be non-negative and equals the number of required repetitions.
a must be a valid parser.
f must be a valid fold function.
da must be a valid destructor for a's outputs.

functions.name: mpc_or
functions.description: Choice: try n alternative parsers in order; succeed with the first that matches.
requirements: n must be the number of parsers passed variadically.
Each variadic argument must be an mpc_parser_t*.

functions.name: mpc_and
functions.description: Sequence: run n parsers in order and fold their results with f.
requirements: n must be the number of subsequent parsers supplied variadically.
f must be a valid fold function.
Each variadic argument must be an mpc_parser_t*.

functions.name: mpc_predictive
functions.description: Enable predictive (no backtracking) behavior for parser a to improve performance and error predictability.
requirements: a must be a valid parser.

functions.name: mpc_eoi
functions.description: Parser that matches end-of-input.

functions.name: mpc_soi
functions.description: Parser that matches start-of-input.

functions.name: mpc_boundary
functions.description: Parser that matches a word boundary (non-alnum to alnum or vice versa).

functions.name: mpc_boundary_newline
functions.description: Parser that matches a boundary considering newline rules (newline-sensitive boundary).

functions.name: mpc_whitespace
functions.description: Parser that matches a single whitespace character.

functions.name: mpc_whitespaces
functions.description: Parser that matches one or more whitespace characters.

functions.name: mpc_blank
functions.description: Parser that matches zero or more whitespace characters (skips blanks).

functions.name: mpc_newline
functions.description: Parser that matches a newline character.

functions.name: mpc_tab
functions.description: Parser that matches a tab character.

functions.name: mpc_escape
functions.description: Parser that matches a C-like escape sequence.

functions.name: mpc_digit
functions.description: Parser that matches a decimal digit [0-9].

functions.name: mpc_hexdigit
functions.description: Parser that matches a hexadecimal digit [0-9A-Fa-f].

functions.name: mpc_octdigit
functions.description: Parser that matches an octal digit [0-7].

functions.name: mpc_digits
functions.description: Parser that matches one or more decimal digits.

functions.name: mpc_hexdigits
functions.description: Parser that matches one or more hexadecimal digits.

functions.name: mpc_octdigits
functions.description: Parser that matches one or more octal digits.

functions.name: mpc_lower
functions.description: Parser that matches a lowercase ASCII letter.

functions.name: mpc_upper
functions.description: Parser that matches an uppercase ASCII letter.

functions.name: mpc_alpha
functions.description: Parser that matches an alphabetic ASCII letter.

functions.name: mpc_underscore
functions.description: Parser that matches the underscore character '_'.

functions.name: mpc_alphanum
functions.description: Parser that matches an alphanumeric ASCII character or underscore.

functions.name: mpc_int
functions.description: Parser that matches a signed integer literal and produces a numeric value.

functions.name: mpc_hex
functions.description: Parser that matches a hexadecimal integer literal and produces a numeric value.

functions.name: mpc_oct
functions.description: Parser that matches an octal integer literal and produces a numeric value.

functions.name: mpc_number
functions.description: Parser that matches a number literal (integer in various bases).

functions.name: mpc_real
functions.description: Parser that matches a real number literal (e.g., with optional sign and decimal point).

functions.name: mpc_float
functions.description: Parser that matches a floating-point literal and produces a numeric value.

functions.name: mpc_char_lit
functions.description: Parser that matches a C-style character literal and produces its value.

functions.name: mpc_string_lit
functions.description: Parser that matches a C-style string literal and produces a string value.

functions.name: mpc_regex_lit
functions.description: Parser that matches a regex literal (syntax per MPC conventions) and produces a corresponding value.

functions.name: mpc_ident
functions.description: Parser that matches an identifier (letter/underscore followed by alphanumerics/underscores).

functions.name: mpc_startwith
functions.description: Parser that ensures input starts with what a matches (anchor to start).
requirements: a must be a valid parser.

functions.name: mpc_endwith
functions.description: Parser that ensures input ends with what a matches (anchor to end), freeing value with da as needed.
requirements: a must be a valid parser.
da must be a valid destructor for a's output or mpcf_dtor_null.

functions.name: mpc_whole
functions.description: Parser that matches a over the entire input (equivalent to soi a eoi), freeing with da as appropriate.
requirements: a must be a valid parser.
da must free values produced by a or be a null-destructor.

functions.name: mpc_stripl
functions.description: Parser that trims leading whitespace from the result of a (left strip) in tokenization workflows.
requirements: a must be a valid parser.

functions.name: mpc_stripr
functions.description: Parser that trims trailing whitespace from the result of a (right strip).
requirements: a must be a valid parser.

functions.name: mpc_strip
functions.description: Parser that trims leading and trailing whitespace around a (strip both sides).
requirements: a must be a valid parser.

functions.name: mpc_tok
functions.description: Token parser that consumes surrounding whitespace around a.
requirements: a must be a valid parser.

functions.name: mpc_sym
functions.description: Parser that matches the exact symbol string s with surrounding tokenization rules.
requirements: s must be a valid NUL-terminated C string.

functions.name: mpc_total
functions.description: Parser that runs a and ensures total consumption of input, cleaning with da if not consumed.
requirements: a must be a valid parser.
da must be a valid destructor for a's value.

functions.name: mpc_between

functions.description: Parser that matches a surrounded by the literal strings o (open) and c (close).
requirements: a must be a valid parser.
ad must be a valid destructor for a's value if needed.
o and c must be valid NUL-terminated strings.

functions.name: mpc_parens
functions.description: Parser that matches a enclosed in parentheses '(...)'.
requirements: a must be a valid parser.
ad must be a valid destructor for a's value.

functions.name: mpc_braces
functions.description: Parser that matches a enclosed in braces '{...}'.
requirements: a must be a valid parser.
ad must be a valid destructor for a's value.

functions.name: mpc_brackets
functions.description: Parser that matches a enclosed in angle brackets '<...>'.
requirements: a must be a valid parser.
ad must be a valid destructor for a's value.

functions.name: mpc_squares
functions.description: Parser that matches a enclosed in square brackets '[...]'.
requirements: a must be a valid parser.
ad must be a valid destructor for a's value.

functions.description: Tokenizing version of between: matches a between strings o and c, consuming surrounding whitespace.
requirements: a must be a valid parser.
ad must be a valid destructor for a's value.
o and c must be valid strings.

functions.name: mpc_tok_parens
functions.description: Tokenizing version of parentheses-delimited a.
requirements: a must be a valid parser.
ad must be a valid destructor for a's value.

functions.name: mpc_tok_braces
functions.description: Tokenizing version of braces-delimited a.
requirements: a must be a valid parser.
ad must be a valid destructor for a's value.

functions.name: mpc_tok_brackets
functions.description: Tokenizing version of angle-bracket-delimited a.
requirements: a must be a valid parser.
ad must be a valid destructor for a's value.

functions.name: mpc_tok_squares
functions.description: Tokenizing version of square-bracket-delimited a.
requirements: a must be a valid parser.
ad must be a valid destructor for a's value.

functions.name: mpc_sepby1
functions.description: Parse one or more occurrences of a separated by sep; fold the collected values with f.
requirements: f must be a valid fold function.
sep and a must be valid parsers.

functions.name: mpcf_dtor_null
functions.description: No-op destructor suitable when no freeing is necessary.
requirements: x may be NULL or any pointer; function does nothing.

functions.name: mpcf_ctor_null
functions.description: Constructor that returns a NULL value placeholder.

functions.name: mpcf_ctor_str
functions.description: Constructor that returns an allocated empty string or string container (exact behavior library-defined).

functions.name: mpcf_free
functions.description: Applier that frees x and returns NULL.
requirements: x must be a pointer previously allocated appropriately (free-able).

functions.name: mpcf_int
functions.description: Applier that converts string x to an integer value object.
requirements: x must point to a suitable representation (commonly a C string).

functions.name: mpcf_hex
functions.description: Applier that converts string x to a hexadecimal integer value object.
requirements: x must point to a suitable representation (commonly a C string).

functions.name: mpcf_oct
functions.description: Applier that converts string x to an octal integer value object.
requirements: x must point to a suitable representation (commonly a C string).

functions.name: mpcf_float
functions.description: Applier that converts string x to a floating-point value object.
requirements: x must point to a suitable representation (commonly a C string).

functions.name: mpcf_strtriml
functions.description: Applier that trims leading whitespace from a string value.
requirements: x must point to a mutable or newly-allocated string representation as expected by MPC.

functions.name: mpcf_strtrimr
functions.description: Applier that trims trailing whitespace from a string value.
requirements: x must point to a suitable string representation.

functions.name: mpcf_strtrim
functions.description: Applier that trims both leading and trailing whitespace from a string value.
requirements: x must point to a suitable string representation.

functions.name: mpcf_escape
functions.description: Applier that escapes characters in a string using C-like escapes.
requirements: x must point to a suitable string value.

functions.name: mpcf_escape_regex
functions.description: Applier that escapes a string for safe use in regex syntax.
requirements: x must point to a suitable string value.

functions.name: mpcf_escape_string_raw
functions.description: Applier that converts a raw string into an escaped representation appropriate for string literals.
requirements: x must point to a suitable string value.

functions.name: mpcf_escape_char_raw
functions.description: Applier that converts a raw character representation into an escaped char literal form.
requirements: x must be a suitable character/short string representation.

functions.name: mpcf_unescape
functions.description: Applier that unescapes C-like escape sequences in a string.
requirements: x must point to a suitable string value.

functions.name: mpcf_unescape_regex
functions.description: Applier that unescapes a regex literal representation to a raw string.
requirements: x must point to a suitable string value.

functions.name: mpcf_unescape_string_raw
functions.description: Applier that converts an escaped string literal into its raw contents.
requirements: x must point to a suitable string value.

functions.name: mpcf_unescape_char_raw
functions.description: Applier that converts an escaped char literal into its raw character value.
requirements: x must be a suitable char/string representation.

functions.name: mpcf_null
functions.description: Fold that ignores inputs and returns NULL.
requirements: n indicates the number of elements in xs and must be consistent.
xs must be a valid array of mpc_val_t* of length at least n.

functions.description: Fold that returns the first element xs[0] without freeing others.
requirements: n must be >= 1.
xs must be a valid array of length at least n.

functions.name: mpcf_snd

requirements: n must be >= 2.
xs must be a valid array of length at least n.

requirements: n must be >= 3.
xs must be a valid array of length at least n.

functions.name: mpcf_fst_free
functions.description: Fold that returns the first element and frees the rest.
requirements: n must be >= 1.
xs must be a valid array of length at least n.

functions.name: mpcf_snd_free

requirements: n must be >= 2.
xs must be a valid array of length at least n.

functions.name: mpcf_trd_free

xs must be a valid array of length at least n.

contents must be a valid C string (may be empty).

functions.name: mpc_ast_build

requirements: n must equal the number of child arguments supplied.
tag must be a valid C string.

functions.name: mpc_ast_add_root
functions.description: Wrap AST a as a new root if required by library conventions, returning the possibly new root.
requirements: a must be a valid AST pointer.

functions.name: mpc_ast_add_child

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for MPC filename strings used as diagnostic labels.
# These are plain NUL-terminated C strings on the C++ side (std::string.c_str()).
# We produce a single bytes buffer that the harness will use for FUZZ_PARAM_STR()
# calls. The buffer should contain interesting but valid UTF-8/ASCII-like content
# resembling filenames or labels, including edge cases such as paths, spaces,
# unicode, long names, extensions, and unusual characters that are still safe.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

# Some interesting filename bases and extensions
BASENAMES = [
    "input", "test", "main", "data", "αβγ", "こんにちは", "пример", "spaced name",
    "tabs\tinside", "newlines\ninside", "dot.start", "..hidden", ".hidden", "NULfree",
    "very-long-name", "emoji-😀", "CON", "NUL", "AUX", "PRN", "COM1", "LPT1",
]
EXTS = ["", ".txt", ".c", ".h", ".json", ".xml", ".md", ".log", ".dat", ".re", ".mpc"]

# Directory components to exercise path handling in diagnostics
DIRS = [
    "", "./", "../", "/", "/tmp/", "C:/", "C:/Windows/", "./dir/", "nested/dir/",
    "ユーザー/", "空间/", "with space/", "dots./", "././", "/var/log/", "relative/./path/",
]

# Suffixes sometimes seen in diagnostics or virtual filenames
SUFFIXES = ["", ":1:1", ":10:20", "(generated)", "<stdin>", "<memory>", "#1", "?query=1", "#fragment"]

SAFE_EXTRA_CHARS = "-_ .@+%^()[]{}!$&=,"  # avoid NUL

# Some Unicode snippets to test wide range but keep valid UTF-8
UNICODE_SNIPS = [
    "µ", "ß", "ø", "ñ", "ç", "å", "汉字", "🙂", "🏳️‍🌈", "Ž", "Ł", "Ђ", "Δ", "Ω"
]


def _rand_choice(r: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return items[r.randrange(len(items))]


def _rand_basename(r: random.Random) -> str:
    base = _rand_choice(r, BASENAMES)
    # Optionally augment with random chars
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        n = r.randint(0, 12)
        extra_pool = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + SAFE_EXTRA_CHARS
        base += ''.join(r.choice(extra_pool) for _ in range(n))
    # Optionally inject a unicode snippet
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        base += _rand_choice(r, UNICODE_SNIPS)
    return base


def _rand_dirpath(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build 0-3 components
    parts = []
    depth = r.randint(0, 3)
    for _ in range(depth):
        parts.append(_rand_choice(r, DIRS))
    # Ensure directory separators are coherent
    path = ''.join(parts)
    return path


def _rand_extension(r: random.Random) -> str:
    return _rand_choice(r, EXTS)


def _rand_suffix(r: random.Random) -> str:
    s = _rand_choice(r, SUFFIXES)
    # Optionally add column/line suffix stack
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        s += f":{r.randint(0, 500)}:{r.randint(0, 200)}"
    return s


def _cap_length(s: str, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Ensure we don't exceed total cap; try to cut at rune boundaries by encoding
    b = s.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')
    if len(b) <= max_len:
        return s
    # Trim bytes and decode ignoring partial edges
    b = b[:max_len]
    return b.decode('utf-8', 'ignore')


def _build_filename(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Compose: optional dirpath + basename + extension + optional suffix
    dirp = _rand_dirpath(r)
    base = _rand_basename(r)
    ext = _rand_extension(r)
    suf = _rand_suffix(r) if r.random() < 0.7 else ""

    # Occasionally create windows-style paths explicitly
    if r.random() < 0.15:
        drive = _rand_choice(r, ["C:", "D:", "Z:"])
        sep = "\\"  # backslashes
        comps = [drive, sep]
        comps.extend([_rand_basename(r) for _ in range(r.randint(0, 3))])
        fname = sep.join([c.strip(sep) for c in comps if c])
        fname = fname.rstrip(sep)
        fname = _cap_length(fname, 240)
        return _cap_length(fname + ext + suf, 512)

    fname = dirp + base + ext + suf
    # Sometimes use angle-bracket virtual names
    if r.random() < 0.1:
        fname = f"<{base}{ext}>"
    # Limit
    return _cap_length(fname, 512)


def _make_cstring_bytes(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Convert to UTF-8 bytes. No embedded NULs here; the harness passes std::string.c_str().
    return s.encode('utf-8')


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Produce between 1 and 6 filename strings concatenated with newlines, so that
    # separate FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls can draw varied content from the same buffer
    # when the harness slices; typical setups consume the whole provided buffer per call,
    # but ensuring variety in a single buffer can help corpus growth.
    count = r.randint(1, 6)
    names = []
    total_budget = MAX_TOTAL - (count - 1)  # account for newlines
    for i in range(count):
        remaining = max(1, total_budget - (count - i - 1))
        # Individual filename budget to keep within cap
        budget = min(512, remaining)
        name = _build_filename(r)
        name = _cap_length(name, budget)
        names.append(name)
        total_budget -= len(name)
    payload = "\n".join(names)

    # Guarantee non-empty and reasonable size
    payload = payload[:MAX_TOTAL]

    return _make_cstring_bytes(payload)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for a generic NUL-terminated C string buffer.
# Target stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR for:
# - parser construction literals (mpc_string, mpc_sym, regex patterns)
# - delimiters (between/tok_between)
# - input filename and input string for mpc_parse
# - values for lift/appliers (numeric strings, escapes, etc.)
# We produce a single bytes blob that the harness splits to serve multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
# The blob will contain a sequence of NUL-terminated slices, each crafted to be valid and
# interesting for MPC: identifiers, whitespace patterns, numbers, regexes, delimiters, failure
# messages, filenames, escaped strings, short char-like snippets, and mixed unicode/bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

IDENT_START = string.ascii_letters + "_"
IDENT_CONT = IDENT_START + string.digits
WS_SET = [" ", "\t", "\r", "\n"]
DIGITS = string.digits
HEX = string.hexdigits
OCT = "01234567"

ESC_SIMPLE = ["\\n", "\\r", "\\t", "\\\\", "\\\"", "\\'", "\\0"]

REGEX_FRAGMENTS = [
    r"[a-z]+",
    r"[A-Z]*",
    r"[0-9]+",
    r"\w+",
    r"\s*",
    r"(foo|bar|baz)",
    r"^start",
    r"end$",
    r"(a.*b)",
    r"(?:he|she)?",
]

SYMBOL_CANDIDATES = ["+", "-", "*", "/", "==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "::", "->", "&&", "||", "::=", "=>"]
DELIM_OPEN = ["(", "{", "[", "<", "/*", "\"", "'", "BEGIN"]
DELIM_CLOSE = [")", "}", "]", ">", "*/", "\"", "'", "END"]

FILENAMES = [
    "input.txt",
    "test.mpc",
    "a/b/c.txt",
    "C:/tmp/file.txt",
    "../relative/path",
    "-virtual-",
]

FAIL_MESSAGES = [
    "expected digit",
    "syntax error",
    "unexpected token",
    "invalid escape",
    "mismatch",
]


def rnd_choice(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str]) -> str:
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]


def gen_ident(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(1, 12)
    s = rng.choice(IDENT_START)
    s += ''.join(rng.choice(IDENT_CONT) for _ in range(n - 1))
    return s


def gen_ws(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(0, 8)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(WS_SET) for _ in range(n))


def gen_int(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    sign = rng.choice(["", "+", "-"])
    body = ''.join(rng.choice(DIGITS) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 8)))
    return sign + body


def gen_hex(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    prefix = rng.choice(["0x", "0X"])
    body = ''.join(rng.choice(HEX) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 6)))
    return prefix + body


def gen_oct(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return "0" + ''.join(rng.choice(OCT) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 6)))


def gen_float(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    sign = rng.choice(["", "+", "-"])
    intp = ''.join(rng.choice(DIGITS) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4)))
    frac = ''.join(rng.choice(DIGITS) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 4)))
    if frac:
        base = f"{intp}.{frac}"
    else:
        base = intp
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        exp = rng.choice(["e", "E"]) + rng.choice(["", "+", "-"]) + ''.join(rng.choice(DIGITS) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)))
    else:
        exp = ""
    return sign + base + exp


def gen_escaped_str(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix raw chars and C escapes
    parts = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 8)):
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            parts.append(rng.choice(ESC_SIMPLE))
        elif rng.random() < 0.1:
            # hex escape \xHH
            hh = ''.join(rng.choice("0123456789abcdef") for _ in range(2))
            parts.append("\\x" + hh)
        else:
            parts.append(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _"))
    return ''.join(parts)


def gen_charish(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # 1-4 bytes, good for char raw appliers
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return rng.choice(string.printable).strip() or "x"
    return ''.join(chr(rng.randint(1, 0x7f)) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4)))


def gen_regex(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build a small but valid regex pattern
    parts = []
    k = rng.randint(1, 4)
    for _ in range(k):
        parts.append(rnd_choice(rng, REGEX_FRAGMENTS))
    # Occasionally add grouping or quantifier
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(rng.choice(["+", "*", "?", "{1,3}"]))
    return ''.join(parts)


def gen_symbol(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return rnd_choice(rng, SYMBOL_CANDIDATES)
    # fallback: punctuation sequence
    punct = "+-*/=<>!&|:%"
    n = rng.randint(1, 4)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(punct) for _ in range(n))


def gen_delims(rng: random.Random) -> (str, str):
    i = rng.randrange(len(DELIM_OPEN))
    return DELIM_OPEN[i], DELIM_CLOSE[i]


def gen_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return rnd_choice(rng, FILENAMES)
    # random-ish name
    return gen_ident(rng) + rnd_choice(rng, [".txt", ".dat", ".c", ".re", ""])  # may be virtual


def segment(tag: str, s: str) -> bytes:
    # Prefix segments with a small label to help diversity in consumers; many consumers ignore, but
    # they only read up to NUL. We include only s and NUL to stay generic.
    return s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore') + b"\x00"


def build_corpus(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    segs: List[bytes] = []

    # Filename for diagnostics
    segs.append(segment("fname", gen_filename(rng)))

    # Input strings for mpc_parse: include several variants
    segs.append(segment("input_ws", gen_ws(rng) + gen_ident(rng)))
    # Numbers
    segs.append(segment("int", gen_int(rng)))
    segs.append(segment("hex", gen_hex(rng)))
    segs.append(segment("oct", gen_oct(rng)))
    segs.append(segment("float", gen_float(rng)))

    # Identifiers and symbols
    segs.append(segment("ident", gen_ident(rng)))
    segs.append(segment("symbol", gen_symbol(rng)))

    # Regex patterns
    segs.append(segment("regex", gen_regex(rng)))

    # Exact strings for mpc_string/mpc_sym
    segs.append(segment("lit_simple", "hello"))
    segs.append(segment("lit_ws", gen_ws(rng) + "token" + gen_ws(rng)))

    # Between/tok_between delimiters
    o, c = gen_delims(rng)
    segs.append(segment("open", o))
    segs.append(segment("close", c))

    # Lift/applier values
    segs.append(segment("esc", gen_escaped_str(rng)))
    segs.append(segment("charish", gen_charish(rng)))

    # Failure messages
    segs.append(segment("fail", rnd_choice(rng, FAIL_MESSAGES)))

    # Additional content-rich lines including newlines and tabs
    segs.append(segment("line", f"{gen_ident(rng)} {gen_symbol(rng)} {gen_int(rng)}\n"))

    # Strings useful for un/escape functions
    segs.append(segment("cstr", '\"' + gen_escaped_str(rng) + '\"'))
    segs.append(segment("chr", "'" + (rng.choice(ESC_SIMPLE) if rng.random() < 0.5 else gen_charish(rng)) + "'"))

    # Some Unicode/UTF-8 content (valid, then NUL-terminated)
    unicode_pool = ["λ", "π", "漢", "🙂", "€", "✓"]
    segs.append(segment("utf8", ''.join(rng.choice(unicode_pool) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4)))))

    # More filenames for other FUZZ_PARAM_STR uses
    segs.append(segment("fname2", gen_filename(rng)))

    return segs


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    segs = build_corpus(rng)

    # Shuffle segments to give varied ordering across seeds while preserving per-seed determinism
    rng.shuffle(segs)

    blob = b"".join(segs)

    # Ensure total size bound and that blob ends with a NUL in case a consumer expects at least one
    if not blob.endswith(b"\x00"):
        blob += b"\x00"

    if len(blob) > MAX_TOTAL:
        blob = blob[:MAX_TOTAL]
        # ensure final NUL-termination after truncation
        if not blob.endswith(b"\x00"):
            blob = blob[:-1] + b"\x00"

    return blob

import random

from typing import List

# This generator targets MPC parse entry points that consume:
# - filename (diagnostic string)
# - input buffer/string (may be arbitrary binary including NUL)
# - implicit length (nparse chooses a sublength)
#
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR is used twice per call site (filename, contents). We will
# return a single bytes blob that encodes two concatenated strings with
# simple length-prefix framing so the harness can split them deterministically.
# Format (little-endian):
# [u16 fname_len][fname_bytes][u16 content_len][content_bytes]
# Both lengths are <= 4096 and bytes may contain any values (including NUL).

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

_fname_corpus = [
    b"stdin",
    b"<memory>",
    b"/dev/stdin",
    b"/tmp/data.txt",
    b"C:/path/to/file.txt",
    b"..",
    b"./a/b/c.lang",
    b"grammar.mpc",
    b"pipe://stream",
    b"unicode_\xce\xbb.txt",
]

_content_corpus = [
    # simple numbers
    b"0", b"-1", b"1234567890", b"+42", b"0xDEADBEEF", b"0o755", b"0755",
    # floats
    b"3.14", b"-0.0", b"6.022e23", b"-1.2e-3", b".5", b"5.",
    # identifiers and tokens
    b"id", b"_start", b"alpha123", b"CamelCase", b"snake_case_1",
    # whitespace variants
    b" \t\n\r\f\v", b"    many    spaces   ", b"\n\n\n",
    # punctuation and delimiters
    b"(){}[]<>", b"(a)[b]{c}<d>", b",;:.", b"a,b;c:d.",
    # quoted strings and escapes
    b"'a'", b"'\\n'", b"\"hello\\nworld\"", b"\"\"", b"'\\x41'", b"'\\101'",
    # string literal with escapes
    b"\"tab\\tquote\\\"backslash\\\\\"",
    # regex-like
    b"/[a-z]+/", b"/\\d{1,3}/i", b"/a.*b/sm", b"/^(foo|bar)$/",
    # boundaries
    b"word boundary", b"foo_bar", b"line1\nline2\n",
    # nested delimiters
    b"(1+(2*3))", b"[a, b, c]", b"{ key: \"val\" }",
    # mixed grammar-like snippets
    b"expr : term ('+' term)*;\nterm : INT | '(' expr ')';\n",
]

_delimited_templates = [
    (b"(", b")"), (b"[", b"]"), (b"{", b"}"), (b"\"", b"\""), (b"'", b"'"), (b"<", b">")
]

# Numeric variant builders returning bytes
_numeric_variants = [
    lambda r: str(r.randint(-(2**31), 2**31 - 1)).encode(),
    lambda r: ("0x%X" % r.getrandbits(32)).encode(),
    lambda r: ("%d.%02d" % (r.randint(-1000, 1000), r.randint(0, 99))).encode(),
    lambda r: ("%de%+d" % (r.randint(1, 999999), r.randint(-50, 50))).encode(),
]

_ident_start = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_"
_ident_body = _ident_start + b"0123456789"


def _rnd_ident(r: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=16) -> bytes:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = bytes([_ident_start[r.randrange(len(_ident_start))]])
    if n > 1:
        s += bytes(_ident_body[r.randrange(len(_ident_body))] for _ in range(n - 1))
    return s


def _rnd_string_lit(r: random.Random, max_len=32) -> bytes:
    # Build a C-like string literal with some escapes
    raw = bytearray()
    n = r.randint(0, max_len)
    # Build escapes lazily since some include random formatting
    for _ in range(n):
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.15:
            esc_choice = r.random()
            if esc_choice < 0.4:
                raw += b"\\n"
            elif esc_choice < 0.6:
                raw += b"\\t"
            elif esc_choice < 0.8:
                raw += b"\\\""
            elif esc_choice < 0.9:
                raw += b"\\\\"
            elif esc_choice < 0.95:
                raw += ("\\x%02X" % r.randrange(256)).encode()
            else:
                raw += ("\\%03o" % r.randrange(256)).encode()
        else:
            ch = r.randrange(32, 126)
            if ch == ord('"'):
                raw += b"\\\""
            else:
                raw.append(ch)
    return b'"' + bytes(raw) + b'"'


def _rnd_char_lit(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    variants = [
        b"'a'",
        b"'\\n'",
        b"'\\t'",
        ("'\\x%02X'" % r.randrange(256)).encode(),
        ("'\\%03o'" % r.randrange(256)).encode(),
    ]
    return r.choice(variants)


def _rnd_regex(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Simple regex literal between slashes with flags
    parts = [b"^", b"$", b".", b"+", b"*", b"?", b"|", b"[a-z]", b"[A-Za-z0-9_]", b"\\d", b"\\w", b"(foo|bar)"]
    k = r.randint(1, 6)
    body = b"".join(r.choice(parts) for _ in range(k))
    flags = b""
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        for f, p in [(b"m", 0.3), (b"s", 0.3)]:
            if r.random() < p:
                flags += f
    return b"/" + body + b"/" + flags


def _rnd_delimited(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    o, c = r.choice(_delimited_templates)
    inner_choices = [
        lambda: _rnd_ident(r),
        lambda: b" ".join(_rnd_ident(r) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3))),
        lambda: b", ".join(_rnd_ident(r) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 4))),
        lambda: _rnd_string_lit(r),
        lambda: _rnd_regex(r),
        lambda: str(r.randint(-100, 100)).encode(),
    ]
    inner = r.choice(inner_choices)()
    return o + inner + c


def _build_contents(r: random.Random, target_max: int) -> bytes:
    segments: List[bytes] = []
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        segments.append(r.choice(_content_corpus))
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6)):
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.15:
            segments.append(_rnd_ident(r))
        elif choice < 0.30:
            segments.append(r.choice(_numeric_variants)(r))
        elif choice < 0.45:
            segments.append(_rnd_string_lit(r))
        elif choice < 0.60:
            segments.append(_rnd_char_lit(r))
        elif choice < 0.75:
            segments.append(_rnd_regex(r))
        else:
            segments.append(_rnd_delimited(r))
        if r.random() < 0.8:
            ws = [b" ", b"\t", b"\n", b",", b";", b"::", b" = ", b" + ", b" - "]
            segments.append(r.choice(ws))
        if sum(len(s) for s in segments) > target_max:
            break
    data = b"".join(segments)
    if not data and r.random() < 0.7:
        data = b"\n"
    if len(data) > target_max:
        data = data[:target_max]
    return data


def _build_filename(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        base = bytearray(r.choice(_fname_corpus))
    else:
        parts = []
        depth = r.randint(1, 4)
        for _ in range(depth):
            if r.random() < 0.2:
                parts.append(b"..")
            else:
                parts.append(_rnd_ident(r, 1, 10))
        base = bytearray(b"/").join(parts)
        exts = [b".txt", b".lang", b".mpc", b".cfg", b".data"]
        if r.random() < 0.7:
            base += r.choice(exts)
        if r.random() < 0.2:
            base = bytearray(b"C:/") + base
    if r.random() < 0.2 and len(base) < max_len - 2:
        base += b"_\xce\xbb"
    if len(base) > max_len:
        base = base[:max_len]
    return bytes(base)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    budget = MAX_TOTAL - 4  # reserve for two u16 lengths
    fname_budget = min(256, max(1, int(budget * 0.15)))
    contents_budget = budget - fname_budget

    fname = _build_filename(r, fname_budget)
    contents = _build_contents(r, contents_budget)

    fname = fname[: min(len(fname), 0xFFFF, fname_budget)]
    contents = contents[: min(len(contents), 0xFFFF, contents_budget)]

    out = bytearray()
    out += struct.pack('<H', len(fname))
    out += fname
    out += struct.pack('<H', len(contents))
    out += contents

    return bytes(out)

# Generator for a valid filesystem path the target will open and read.
# We create a small text-like file content inside the buffer and encode a
# virtual filename scheme that the fuzz harness maps to an on-disk temp file.
# Many fuzzers that provide FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() understand inputs like:
#   name\0filedata...
# or use a simple path-only buffer. Since we cannot rely on harness specifics,
# we generate just a plausible path string and let the fuzzer map it to a file.
# To increase meaningful coverage, we sometimes embed directories and different
# extensions that typical parsers may react to, while keeping it under 4096 bytes.

SAFE_DIRS = [
    ".", "./", "./data/", "./inputs/", "./tmp/", "/tmp/", "/var/tmp/"
]
BASENAMES = [
    "input", "sample", "test", "prog", "expr", "number", "string",
    "regex", "ident", "grammar", "script", "conf", "data", "file"
]
EXTS = [
    "", ".txt", ".dat", ".in", ".mpc", ".cfg", ".gram", ".re", ".str"
]

# Optional subdirectories to vary traversal and edge cases (no symlinks or absolute ups)
SUBDIRS = [
    "", "a/", "b/", "nested/", "deep/n1/", "deep/n1/n2/"
]

# To hint at interesting content, we optionally add suffix tokens that tools sometimes special-case
SUFFIXES = [
    "", "-ascii", "-utf8", "-latin1", "-large", "-small", "-zero", "-eoi", "-soi"
]


def _choose_weighted(rng: random.Random, items: List[str], weights: List[int]) -> str:
    total = sum(weights)
    pick = rng.randrange(total)
    acc = 0
    for item, w in zip(items, weights):
        acc += w
        if pick < acc:
            return item
    return items[-1]


def _rand_basename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    base = rng.choice(BASENAMES)
    # Add numeric and mixed tokens to avoid collisions and explore branches
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        base += str(rng.randrange(0, 1000000))
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        base += rng.choice(["_", "-", "."]) + rng.choice(BASENAMES)
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        base += rng.choice(SUFFIXES)
    return base


def _rand_extension(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Prefer common text-like extensions
    return _choose_weighted(rng, EXTS, [1, 5, 3, 3, 4, 3, 3, 2, 2])


def _rand_dir(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Prefer relative safe directories that fuzz harnesses often create
    d = _choose_weighted(rng, SAFE_DIRS, [4, 5, 3, 3, 3, 2, 1])
    if not d.endswith("/") and d not in (".", "./"):
        d += "/"
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        d += rng.choice(SUBDIRS)
    return d


def _make_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    d = _rand_dir(rng)
    name = _rand_basename(rng)
    ext = _rand_extension(rng)
    path = f"{d}{name}{ext}"
    # Clamp length
    if len(path) > 256:
        path = path[:256]
    # Avoid trailing slash only path
    if path.endswith("/"):
        path = path[:-1] + "_"
    # Ensure it's a clean C string without NULs
    path = path.replace("\x00", "_")
    return path


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Sometimes choose very simple names to exercise short-path branches
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        simple = rng.choice([
            "input.txt", "a", "in", "t.txt", "0", "1", "file", "data.txt"
        ])
        return simple.encode("utf-8")

    path = _make_path(rng)

    # Bias towards existing-ish tmp locations if harness maps paths directly
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        path = "/tmp/" + os.path.basename(path)

    # Keep under 4096 bytes
    b = path.encode("utf-8")[:4096]
    return b

# Target data type: identifier/name string for mpc_new(name.c_str())
# We generate a NUL-terminated-friendly byte buffer that FUZZ_PARAM_STR likely
# reads entirely to construct a std::string. We therefore place interesting
# ASCII identifiers, unicode, long names, empty and special characters, while
# keeping inputs valid C-strings (no embedded NUL), since mpc_new expects
# a NUL-terminated C string and will stop at the first NUL. We avoid NUL bytes.
#
# Strategy:
# - Choose from several crafted name classes to exercise different code paths:
#   * Simple identifiers (alpha/underscore start, alnum/_ rest)
#   * Names with separators or namespace-like scopes ("::", ".", "/")
#   * Names including whitespace or punctuation (still valid bytes for C-string)
#   * Mixed case, digits, very long names near typical limits
#   * Unicode (UTF-8) sequences to stress non-ASCII handling in consumers
#   * Edge cases: empty string, single-char, repeated chars
# - Ensure no NUL bytes in the payload; size cap <= 4096 bytes.
# - Randomized but deterministic via seed.

MAX_LEN = 4096

ASCII_LETTERS = string.ascii_letters
IDENT_START = string.ascii_letters + "_"
IDENT_CONT = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"
SEP_CHARS = ["::", ".", "/", "-", ":", "@"]
PUNCT = "-.:,@+$%^&*=~"  # avoid NUL and pathologically problematic bytes
WS = [" ", "\t"]

# Some UTF-8 codepoint ranges to sample from (multibyte, non-NUL):
UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "αβγ",            # Greek
    "漢字",            # CJK
    "élève",          # Latin accents
    "नाम",           # Devanagari
    "имя",            # Cyrillic
    "✨",              # emoji (multi-byte)
]


def _rand_ident(r: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 32) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    start = r.choice(IDENT_START)
    rest = "".join(r.choice(IDENT_CONT) for _ in range(max(0, n - 1)))
    return start + rest


def _rand_namespaced(r: random.Random) -> str:
    parts = [
        _rand_ident(r, 1, r.randint(1, 12)) for _ in range(r.randint(2, 5))
    ]
    sep = r.choice(SEP_CHARS)
    return sep.join(parts)


def _rand_with_punct(r: random.Random) -> str:
    base = _rand_ident(r, 1, r.randint(3, 24))
    inserts = r.randint(1, 4)
    for _ in range(inserts):
        pos = r.randint(0, len(base))
        base = base[:pos] + r.choice(PUNCT + r.choice(WS)) + base[pos:]
    return base


def _long_name(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Produce a long but bounded identifier-like name
    target = r.randint(200, min(1024, MAX_LEN - 1))
    chunks: List[str] = []
    while sum(len(c) for c in chunks) < target:
        choice = r.randint(0, 2)
        if choice == 0:
            chunks.append(_rand_ident(r, 3, 16))
        elif choice == 1:
            chunks.append(r.choice(SEP_CHARS))
        else:
            # occasional punctuation or whitespace
            chunks.append(r.choice(PUNCT + " "))
    s = "".join(chunks)
    return s[:target]


def _unicode_name(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix ascii identifier with a unicode sample
    parts = []
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 5)):
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append(_rand_ident(r, 1, 8))
        else:
            parts.append(r.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES))
    return r.choice(["::", "/", ".", "-"]).join(parts)


def _edge_case(r: random.Random) -> str:
    cases = [
        "",                 # empty name
        "_",                # single underscore
        "a",                # single letter
        "0name",            # starts with digit (still a valid string for mpc_new)
        "__proto__",        # common special-ish
        "default",          # keyword-like
        "name with spaces", # includes spaces
        "tab\tname",        # includes tab
        "trail-space ",
        "lead-space ",
    ]
    return r.choice(cases)


def _sanitize(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Ensure no NULs and limit size
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    b = b.replace(b"\x00", b"")
    return b[: MAX_LEN]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a class with weighted probabilities
    generators = [
        (0.22, _rand_ident),
        (0.18, _rand_namespaced),
        (0.18, _rand_with_punct),
        (0.16, _long_name),
        (0.16, _unicode_name),
        (0.10, _edge_case),
    ]

    p = r.random()
    cum = 0.0
    chosen = generators[-1][1]
    for w, g in generators:
        cum += w
        if p <= cum:
            chosen = g
            break

    if chosen is _rand_ident:
        s = chosen(r, 1, r.randint(1, 48))
    else:
        s = chosen(r)

    # Guarantee non-empty sometimes to avoid empty dominating:
    if len(s) == 0 and r.random() < 0.6:
        s = _rand_ident(r, 1, 8)

    # Final sanitize and ensure non-NUL bytes only
    out = _sanitize(s)

    # Ensure non-empty bytes if requested and still empty after sanitize
    if not out:
        out = b"nonempty"

    return out

# Generator for MPC character set strings used by mpc_oneof/mpc_noneof.
# We produce a single NUL-terminated buffer containing a non-empty set string.

# Goals:
# - Always non-empty to pass stub checks
# - Include diverse characters: ASCII classes, escapes, whitespace, digits, letters, punctuation
# - Sometimes include duplicates, ranges-like sequences, and multibyte UTF-8 (permissible as bytes)
# - Length kept reasonable (< 4096)

_MAX_LEN = 256

_ASCII_WHITESPACE = " \t\r\n\v\f"
_ASCII_PUNCT = "!\"#$%&'()*+,-./:;<=>?@[\\]^_`{|}~"

_ASCII_DIGITS = string.digits
_COMMON_SETS = [
    "a",                     # single
    "ab",                    # small
    "01",                    # binary
    "0123456789",            # digits
    string.hexdigits,         # hex
    string.ascii_lowercase,   # lower
    string.ascii_uppercase,   # upper
    string.ascii_letters,     # letters
    string.ascii_letters + string.digits,  # alnum
    _ASCII_WHITESPACE,        # whitespace
    _ASCII_PUNCT,             # punctuation
    string.printable.strip(), # printable (no space)
    "\n\t ",                 # common ws mix

# Some UTF-8 multibyte code points to include occasionally.
_UTF8_SNIPPETS = [

]

def _weighted_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str], weights: List[int]) -> str:
    total = sum(weights)
    pick = rng.randrange(total)
    acc = 0
    for item, w in zip(items, weights):
        acc += w
        if pick < acc:
            return item
    return items[-1]

def _make_set_from_palette(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build a set by sampling from multiple palettes
    palettes = [
        _ASCII_WHITESPACE,
        _ASCII_PUNCT,
        _ASCII_LETTERS,
        _ASCII_DIGITS,
        string.printable,
    ]
    # Start with a base common set sometimes
    s = rng.choice(_COMMON_SETS) if rng.random() < 0.6 else ""

    # Add random samples from palettes
    rounds = rng.randint(1, 5)
    for _ in range(rounds):
        pal = rng.choice(palettes)
        k = rng.randint(1, 10)
        s += "".join(rng.choice(pal) for _ in range(k))

    # Occasionally add UTF-8 characters
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
            s += rng.choice(_UTF8_SNIPPETS)

    # Occasionally add duplicates and sequential patterns
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        c = rng.choice(string.printable)
        s += c * rng.randint(2, 6)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # range-like sequence (still literal chars in set)
        start = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits)
        step = 1 if rng.random() < 0.7 else -1
        length = rng.randint(3, 8)
        seq = []
        cur = ord(start)
        for _ in range(length):
            # stay within visible ASCII range
            if 48 <= cur <= 122:
                seq.append(chr(cur))
            cur += step
        s += "".join(seq)

    # Shuffle to avoid predictable order
    lst = list(s)
    rng.shuffle(lst)
    s = "".join(lst)

    # Trim length
    if len(s) == 0:
        s = "x"
    if len(s) > _MAX_LEN:
        s = s[:_MAX_LEN]
    return s

def _maybe_escape_c_style(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    # Sometimes introduce backslashes and common escapes literally into the set
    # These are literal backslash and following char; MPC treats set as raw chars.
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        escapes = ["\\n", "\\t", "\\r", "\\0", "\\\\", "\\'", '\\"']
        inserts = rng.randint(1, 4)
        for _ in range(inserts):
            pos = rng.randrange(len(s)+1)
            esc = rng.choice(escapes)
            s = s[:pos] + esc + s[pos:]
        # Trim if too long
        if len(s) > _MAX_LEN:
            s = s[:_MAX_LEN]
    return s

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a generation strategy
    strategies = [
        "common",   # pick from predefined common sets
        "palette",  # build from palettes
        "mixed",    # mix and escape
    ]
    strat = _weighted_choice(rng, strategies, [3, 5, 4])

    if strat == "common":
        s = rng.choice(_COMMON_SETS)
        # Possibly add a few random extras
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            extras = "".join(rng.choice(string.printable) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 8)))
            s += extras
    elif strat == "palette":
        s = _make_set_from_palette(rng)
    else:  # mixed
        s = _make_set_from_palette(rng)
        s = _maybe_escape_c_style(rng, s)

    # Ensure non-empty and within size limit
    if not s:
        s = "A"
    if len(s) > _MAX_LEN:
        s = s[:_MAX_LEN]

    # Return as bytes; FUZZ_PARAM_STR expects a buffer; harness will NUL-terminate when converting to C string
    # We provide no explicit NUL inside to avoid premature termination; content may include backslashes and UTF-8.
    data = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    # Hard cap to 4096
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: human-readable message (NUL-terminated C string semantics)
# Fuzzer stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR for:
# - mpc_fail: requires a non-empty message string.
# - mpc_expect: requires a non-empty error message string.
# - Building an mpc_err_t*: uses three strings: failure message, filename, input string.
#   filename and input can be empty in general, but providing diverse, valid strings
#   exercises paths in diagnostics and state handling.
# Our strategy: build a single buffer that concatenates several candidate strings separated
# by NUL (\0). The harness can read successive FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls from the same buffer
# if it is configured that way; if not, at least each pull gets a valid non-empty string
# early in the buffer. We ensure:
# - Multiple messages of varying content and length.
# - Inclusion of ASCII, Unicode (UTF-8), whitespace, punctuation, format specifiers, regex-like,
#   path-like strings for filename, and typical parser inputs (numbers, identifiers, brackets, etc.).
# - All strings are NUL-terminated; the overall buffer is <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

_PRESETS_MESSAGES = [
    "error: unexpected token",
    "invalid syntax",
    "parse failed",
    "expected identifier",
    "unterminated string literal",
    "division by zero",
    "overflow in numeric literal",
    "custom failure: %s at %d",
]

_PRESETS_FILENAMES = [
    "input.txt",
    "stdin",
    "<memory>",
    "path/with spaces/file.mpc",
    "../relative/path/file",
    "C:/Windows/Temp/tmp.txt",
]

_PRESETS_INPUTS = [
    "",  # allow empty input sometimes
    "hello",
    "12345",
    "-42",
    "0xDEADbeef",
    "0755",
    "3.14159",
    "identifier_name",
    "(a+b)*c - 5",
    "[1, 2, 3]",
    "{ key: ""value"" }",
    "'c'\n\t\r",
    "regex:/[A-Z]+\d*/",
    "alpha beta\tgamma\ndelta",
]

_UTF8_SNIPPETS = [
    "Ω≈ç√∫˜µ≤≥÷",
    "你好，世界",
    "Привет мир",
    "こんにちは世界",
    "🙂🙃🎯",
]

_FORMAT_SPECIFIERS = [
    "%s",
    "%d",
    "%f",
    "%08x",
    "%.*s",
]

_REGEXY = [
    "^([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)$",
    "\n+|\s*#.*$",
    "(foo|bar){1,3}?",
]

_PATHY = [
    "/tmp/test.input",
    "./grammar.lang",
    "../data/sample.txt",
]

_WHITESPACES = [
    " ",
    "\t",
    "\n",
    " \t \n",
]

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length)).strip('\x00')
    # Ensure non-empty after stripping NULs
    if not s:
        s = "A"
    return s

def _maybe_mix(rng: random.Random, base: str, extras: List[str]) -> str:
    parts = [base]
    for e in extras:
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            parts.append(e)
    return ' '.join(parts)

def _make_message(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.25:
        msg = rng.choice(_PRESETS_MESSAGES)
    elif choice < 0.5:
        msg = _maybe_mix(rng, rng.choice(_PRESETS_MESSAGES), [rng.choice(_FORMAT_SPECIFIERS)])
    elif choice < 0.75:
        msg = rng.choice(_UTF8_SNIPPETS) + ": " + rng.choice(_PRESETS_MESSAGES)
    else:
        msg = _rand_ascii(rng, 5, 60)
    # Ensure non-empty for mpc_fail/mpc_expect
    if not msg:
        msg = "failure"
    return msg

def _make_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    pool = _PRESETS_FILENAMES + _PATHY
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        # random pathy string
        base = _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 20).replace('\x00', '')
        base = ''.join(c if c not in '\\:\n\r\t' else '_' for c in base)
        return f"/var/fuzz/{base}.txt"
    return rng.choice(pool)

def _make_input(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.5:
        s = rng.choice(_PRESETS_INPUTS)
    else:
        # Compose a small expression/sequence
        tokens = [
            rng.choice(["foo", "bar", "baz", "qux", "id_", "var"]) + str(rng.randint(0, 99)),
            rng.choice(["+", "-", "*", "/", "==", "!=", "<=", ">="]),
            rng.choice([str(rng.randint(-999, 999)), hex(rng.randint(0, 0xFFFF)), str(rng.random())]),
        ]
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            tokens.insert(0, rng.choice(["(", "[", "{"]) + rng.choice(_WHITESPACES))
            tokens.append(rng.choice(_WHITESPACES) + rng.choice([")", "]", "}"]))
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            tokens.append(rng.choice([",", ";"]))
        s = ' '.join(tokens)
    # Occasionally add regexy or utf8 snippet to stress tokenizer
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        s += " " + rng.choice(_REGEXY)
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        s += " " + rng.choice(_UTF8_SNIPPETS)
    return s

def _pack_cstrs(strs: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Join with NUL terminators; ensure final NUL for the last one
    b = bytearray()
    for s in strs:
        bs = s.encode('utf-8', errors='replace')
        # Avoid embedded NULs inside strings to preserve C-string semantics
        if b"\x00" in bs:
            bs = bs.replace(b"\x00", b" ")
        b += bs + b"\x00"
        if len(b) >= MAX_TOTAL:
            break
    return bytes(b[:MAX_TOTAL])

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a pool of strings that FUZZ_PARAM_STR can draw from in sequence:
    # We include several messages first to satisfy non-empty requirements of mpc_fail/mpc_expect.
    cstrs: List[str] = []

    # Ensure at least two non-empty messages for mpc_fail and mpc_expect
    cstrs.append(_make_message(rng))
    cstrs.append(_make_message(rng))

    # Add a plausible filename and input for the error-producing stub
    cstrs.append(_make_filename(rng))
    cstrs.append(_make_input(rng))

    # Add extra diversity to increase coverage for subsequent FUZZ_PARAM_STR pulls
    extra_count = rng.randint(4, 12)
    for _ in range(extra_count):
        kind = rng.random()
        if kind < 0.4:
            cstrs.append(_make_message(rng))
        elif kind < 0.7:
            cstrs.append(_make_filename(rng))
        else:
            cstrs.append(_make_input(rng))

    buf = _pack_cstrs(cstrs)

    # Guarantee size constraints and non-emptiness
    if not buf:
        buf = b"default\x00"
    elif len(buf) > MAX_TOTAL:
        buf = buf[:MAX_TOTAL]

    return buf
